findings.title: Unauthenticated requests can create unlimited topics and outbound fetches
Imported HTML stored and rendered unsanitized (stored XSS)
findings.body:
Posts imported from RSS/Atom (`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content)`) or via readability are created with `cook_method: raw_html`. `Post#cook` then returns `raw` verbatim, with no sanitization. The rendered post is output with `raw post.cooked` in the embed view and on the forum.

Risks:
- Any script, event handler, or `javascript:` href in the feed or remote page runs in the forum's origin.
- Readability keeps `href`, so `javascript:` URLs survive that path too.
- Any later edit to such a post (by a moderator or the author) also bypasses cooking and sanitization.
- The 'imported from' footer interpolates `url` into an HTML attribute without escaping.

The content should be sanitized before storage or rendering.

findings.title: `<%- end if %>` typo breaks template compilation/logic
findings.body: The header conditional is closed with `<%- end if %>` instead of `<%- end %>`. In compiled ERB, `end if` turns the next generated statement into an `if` modifier condition, or produces a syntax error, depending on how the buffer append is emitted. Either way the template is broken or the logo link output becomes conditional unexpectedly.

findings.title: Feed items without `content` crash the whole poll
findings.body: `i.content.scrub` assumes every item has a `content` element. Plain RSS feeds normally use `description`, and Atom entries may only have a summary. For such items `i.content` is nil, which raises NoMethodError and aborts the import of all remaining items. Retries are disabled, so the poll simply fails every hour. `i.title` may also be nil. The code should fall back to description/summary and skip items with no content.

findings.title: Kernel#open on a setting allows command execution
findings.body: `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses Kernel#open, which spawns a shell command when the string starts with `|`. An admin setting can therefore be escalated to arbitrary command execution on the server. `import_remote` uses the same `open(url)` pattern, including in the disqus importer on file-provided links. Use `URI.parse(url).open` or an HTTP client restricted to http/https instead.

findings.title: Re-import crashes if the embedded post or topic was deleted
findings.body:
When an embed already exists, `post = embed.post` is passed straight to `PostRevisor.new(post).revise!`. If moderators deleted the post, the `belongs_to` lookup returns nil and `revise!` raises NoMethodError. Each hourly feed poll for that item would then fail.

Similarly, `topic_id_for_embed` still returns the id of a deleted topic, so the embed endpoint builds a `TopicView` for it and errors instead of showing the page.

findings.title: Non-atomic SETNX + EXPIRE throttle
findings.body: The throttle calls `setnx` and then `expire` as two separate commands. If the process dies between them, the key never expires and that URL is permanently throttled. Use `SET key 1 NX EX 60` atomically.

findings.title: import_remote relies on open-uri being loaded elsewhere
findings.body: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url)` with an http URL but never requires 'open-uri'. It only works if poll_feed.rb (or something else) has already been loaded. Otherwise `open` treats the URL as a local file path and raises ENOENT, for example in the disqus thor task or in TopicRetriever when feed polling is disabled.

findings.title: "404 without an embed_url" test passes for the wrong reason
findings.body: No `embeddable_host` is stubbed in this test, so `ensure_embeddable` raises InvalidAccess before `params.require(:embed_url)` is ever reached. The test passes regardless of how a missing embed_url is handled. The same pattern affects poll_feed_spec: the url/username tests pass only because `feed_polling_enabled` defaults to false.
